solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Aliens whizz by sun, turning to achieve downward mobility

indicators.note: turning round the whole string means it is read from the end back to the start

parts.note: ETs are extraterrestrials, crossword aliens
a whizz is an expert, an ace
Sol is the Latin name of the sun

explanation.surface: Visiting aliens zipping past the sun suddenly start sinking in the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses the whole chain ETS + ACE + SOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to drop in social standing, originally by breaking the rules of one's Hindu caste, is to move downwards in society.

clue.text: Circle and cross used in international form of language

indicators.note: the circle-and-cross pair is placed within the international player's word

parts.note: a Lion is a player for the British and Irish Lions, a touring international rugby team
O is shaped like a circle
to cut is to cross or intersect, as roads do

explanation.surface: Looks like instructions for drawing symbols in some universal script.
explanation.walkthrough: The British and Irish Lions are a rugby side picked from four nations, so any Lion is an 'international'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a particular phrase or style of expression is a manner of speaking.

clue.text: Promised to keep mulberry plant on sale, but not mint?

indicators.note: the word for promised holds the plant within it, keeping it

parts.note: sworn means pledged or promised
the hop was classed in the mulberry family

explanation.surface: A vendor vowing to hold back a mulberry bush for sale, though it is not in perfect condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mint' here means in pristine condition, not the herb the plant talk suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: goods that have sat in a store being handled are faded and no longer in perfect condition.

clue.text: Conventional form of French words with capitals raised

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising letters means reading them upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: mots is French for words
UC stands for upper case, capital letters

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a convention for writing French with capital letters lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses MOTS + UC as a whole, which suits a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a habitual practice or tradition is the accepted, conventional way of doing something.

clue.text: Stones below Cliff before number is broadcast

indicators.note: in the down entry, the stones come before the number

parts.note: scree is the loose stone debris at a cliff foot

explanation.surface: Suggests a Rolling Stones and Cliff Richard pop show going on air.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital C makes 'Cliff' look like Cliff Richard, a British pop singer, alongside the Rolling Stones band, but it is a rock face.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to show a programme on television is to air or transmit it.

clue.text: Gas dye we sprayed on the side

indicators.note: sprayed suggests the letters are scattered about and land in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone spraying gas and dye on the side of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: sideways, with the side or edge leading, as in getting a word in sideways.

clue.text: In LA, my ditching husband is contemptible

indicators.note: ditching means dropping the husband's letter from the exclamation

parts.note: shucks is an American exclamation like 'my!', as one might say in Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A Los Angeles woman grumbles that a husband who ditches her is a contemptible man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In LA' flags an American word; 'my' is the exclamation, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang: to say something is lousy or awful is to call it worthless and despicable.

clue.text: Mountain or lake said to provide cover for some below primates

indicators.note: said signals that the word for the excess is spoken and what is heard is entered

parts.note: an EU butter mountain or wine lake was a huge excess of produce

explanation.surface: Reads like a geography question about which peak or lake shelters creatures beneath the apes.
explanation.walkthrough: Primates here are archbishops, senior clergy; those below them wear the vestment. The butter mountains and wine lakes were European farm gluts of the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a loose white linen vestment is worn over the cassock by clergy and choristers.

clue.text: Always forgetting last time, spiteful woman set fire to bed cloth

indicators.note: each of the three words loses its final letter, a T, the time abbreviation

parts.note: a cat is a spiteful woman
lit means set fire to
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A vindictive woman, again, burns a bed cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Always forgetting last time' drops T (time) from the end of every piece, leaving CA, LI and CO.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a plain cotton fabric, originally from Calicut in India, is a kind of textile.

clue.text: Tight connection between seconds and years

indicators.note: between puts the connection in the middle, with seconds on one side and years on the other

parts.note: a link is a connection

explanation.surface: A time-span puzzle: a close bond linking seconds and years.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a dress that clings closely to the body is figure-hugging, close-fitting.

clue.text: Councillor storing nothing in socks, a role denied to beggar?

indicators.note: the councillor's abbreviation stores the rest inside it
nothing sits inside the socks

parts.note: hose are socks or stockings
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A councillor hoarding nothing in his socks, a part no beggar may play.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition rests on the proverb 'beggars can't be choosers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the proverb says the poor cannot be those who select; they must take what they are given.

clue.text: Blighted in pox, meet a kind of immunity

indicators.note: blighted means spoiled, so the letters are ruined into a new order

explanation.surface: Meeting someone who has the pox brings a kind of disease protection.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being freed from a duty or tax is a form of immunity from it.

clue.text: One name adopted by citizen under Caesar, who's very powerful

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the name letter is taken into the citizen's word, adopted into its family

parts.note: a Roman was a citizen of Caesar's empire

explanation.surface: A man taking a name to become a Roman citizen under a powerful ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a person of great physical strength and stamina, like a triathlete, is a tough, mighty figure.

clue.text: Support allowance from Area 51 funds, hiding first of extraterrestrials

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: the funds hide away, losing, one letter

parts.note: money means funds

indicators.note: first of picks the initial letter of the word

explanation.surface: Area 51, the US base of alien-sighting lore, paying out benefit while concealing the aliens.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: payment made to a former spouse after divorce is a maintenance allowance.

clue.text: NCO job consists of shutting up soldiers and barking

parts.note: noncom is short for a non-commissioned officer

indicators.note: the job shuts the soldiers up inside it

parts.note: a post is a job
men are ordinary soldiers
is, as in 'the team is eleven players', means consists of

explanation.surface: A sergeant's duty is locking up the troops and shouting orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' looks like shouting, but here it is British slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin legal phrase meaning not of sound mind, which matches British slang for crazy.

clue.text: Cancelling factors at first, five/zero's worked out very large

indicators.note: worked out means the remaining letters are rearranged
cancelling strikes out a letter, as one cancels a factor in a fraction
at first picks the initial letter of the word

explanation.surface: Maths homework: cancel the factors in five over zero and work out the result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cancelling' removes F, the first of factors, from FIVEZEROS, leaving IVEZEROS for 'worked out' to rearrange. Dividing five by zero would be infinitely large.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: bigger than the usual measure, outsize or huge.

clue.text: Muscle exercises court dictated?

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercises
oral means spoken, as dictated words are

explanation.surface: Asks whether workouts at the court are prescribed for a muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the chest muscles are known as 'pecs', by name from the Latin for breast.

clue.text: Cause of much discomfort right inside roomy vehicle

indicators.note: the right abbreviation sits inside the vehicle's word

parts.note: a tourer is a car with space for touring

explanation.surface: Sitting right inside a spacious car is surprisingly uncomfortable.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: one who inflicts pain on others causes them great suffering.

clue.text: Second high point of sale: further reduction of 24 assumed

parts.note: up means high
POS stands for point of sale

indicators.note: the forename in 24, already a short form, is cut down again to two letters

parts.note: 24 points to the across answer, the comedian Murphy's forename

explanation.surface: A retail note: the second peak of a sale, assumed to bring further price cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward shortens to the name in 24, which shortens again to ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: taken for granted or presumed to be true without proof.

clue.text: Scorer cut leg in sudden attack, missing finish

indicators.note: the shortened leg goes inside the shortened attack
missing finish removes the last letter

parts.note: a pounce is a sudden attack

indicators.note: cut trims the last letter off the word

parts.note: leg taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A goal-scorer injured in a sudden tackle and unable to finish the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scorer' is a writer of musical scores, not a footballer: Francis Poulenc, the French composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a French composer of the twentieth century is one who writes musical scores.

clue.text: Spot tart up on fringes of Lanzarote

parts.note: to pimp is to tart up or embellish flashily

indicators.note: fringes of takes the outer letters of the word

explanation.surface: A blemish dolled up on the edges of a Canary Island holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a small spot or blemish on the skin, a zit.

clue.text: Possibly fell and died after united plot

indicators.note: died is placed after the other pieces

parts.note: a plan is a plot or scheme

explanation.surface: Someone may have fallen and died after a joint conspiracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' is not the verb: a fell is a hill or moor in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: high moorland in northern England, a hill, is elevated ground.

clue.text: Sort of rapid or overhead delivery?

indicators.note: sort means to put in order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks what kind of speedy delivery service, rapid or through the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: supplies parachuted down from an aircraft come from above.

clue.text: Start being shot in battle

parts.note: Act I is the first act, the start of a play
on as in on camera, being filmed

explanation.surface: A soldier is shot as fighting starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start being shot' calls up the director's cry on a film set, but it is two pieces: ACT I and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: military combat, as in being killed in a fight.

clue.text: Pole's carrier whose mutation could be random

indicators.note: a mutation is a change of form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks who carries a pole, with a name that scrambles into a random word.
explanation.walkthrough: Printed as wordplay in reverse: the answer mutated would be 'random'. 'Pole' is a surveying staff, not a Polish person.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a surveyor's assistant holds the levelling staff upright for sightings.

clue.text: Sweetened beer gets the most out of solicitor

parts.note: to milk is to exploit fully
a tout solicits custom, as for tickets

explanation.surface: A beer drinker wringing every advantage from a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' is not the British lawyer but one who solicits.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a dark ale brewed with lactose has a sweetish taste.

clue.text: It's unusual in house with one party wall, backing walls up

indicators.note: backing means the whole is turned round and read from the end
the odd word goes inside the house

parts.note: a semi, semi-detached house, shares one wall with its neighbour
rum is British slang for odd or unusual

explanation.surface: Something odd in a semi-detached house where the walls are being rebuilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with one party wall' belongs to the house, not the definition: a semi-detached home shares one wall. 'backing' reverses SERUMMI.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to enclose or imprison someone within walls is to wall them in.

clue.text: Murphy, perhaps as part of balanced diet

indicators.note: as part of says the name lies inside the run of letters

explanation.surface: Murphy (a potato) seemingly as part of a healthy balanced diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Murphy' looks like the slang for a potato, but the surname calls for the comedian's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the American comic actor Murphy has this first name.

clue.text: Soviet city's tendency to dismiss a radical

indicators.note: to dismiss means the letter is sent away from the word

parts.note: a leaning is a tendency

explanation.surface: A Soviet city inclined to get rid of a radical.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: St Petersburg bore this name during the Soviet period.
